primary_hypothesis.H1: Gold existed at the Kamil target before the impact and was subsequently melted, entrained or encapsulated in impact glass.

submodels.H1A_NATURAL_TERRESTRIAL: Pre-impact terrestrial gold was present in target/colluvial material.
submodels.H1B_ANTHROPOGENIC: Pre-impact worked gold/electrum or gilded material was present at the surface and was engulfed by impact melt.

null_and_controls.H0_METEORITIC: Detected Au derives from the Gebel Kamil projectile, whose bulk Au is about 1.57 ppm.
null_and_controls.H0_MIXED: Au occurs in mixed target-projectile melt and covaries with projectile tracers Ni, Co, Pt, Ir and Fe-Ni metal blebs.
null_and_controls.H0_BACKGROUND: Trace terrestrial Au occurs at ordinary crustal/background levels without archaeological significance.

geological_constraint.surface_target: Lower Cretaceous Gilf Kebir Formation quartz-arenite sandstone with minor ferruginous beds plus shallow colluvium/eolian sand.
geological_constraint.basement: Precambrian crystalline basement occurs regionally but published crater/ejecta studies report that the Kamil impact did not excavate basement rocks.
geological_constraint.consequence: Any pre-impact gold incorporated into Kamil impact glass must have been present in the shallow sedimentary/colluvial target or in material/objects lying at or near the pre-impact surface; a deep-basement gold source is not supported by the crater excavation geometry.

highest_value_test.reason: Published major/trace-element work identifies white glass as virtually pure target-sandstone melt with negligible projectile contamination compared with dark glass.
highest_value_test.prediction_if_preimpact_gold: Au enrichment in white glass, target clasts or pre-impact sandstone that does not scale with projectile Ni-Co-Pt-Ir signatures.
highest_value_test.prediction_if_meteoritic_gold: Au should preferentially track projectile-rich dark glass, Fe-Ni blebs and meteoritic siderophile-element patterns.

positive_features: Au-rich domains many orders above the projectile ppm-scale baseline
Au-Ag or Au-Ag-Cu alloy compositions compatible with ancient Egyptian gold/electrum rather than Fe-Ni meteoritic metal
foil, sheet, wire, solder seam, hammered/worked texture, repeated thickness or geometric edge surviving partial melting
spatially repeated gold-rich inclusions inconsistent with random projectile droplets
archaeological material directly enclosed by glass or welded to shocked target rock
anthropogenic_gold_discriminator.caution: Ancient Egyptian alluvial gold can itself contain PGE inclusions, so the presence of Pt-group minerals alone is not sufficient evidence of meteoritic origin. Projectile-specific elemental covariance and metallurgical texture are required.

measurement_order: Micro-CT of archived white and dark glass to locate high-density inclusions non-destructively.
Micro-XRF maps for Au-Ag-Cu-Ni-Co-Fe-Pt/Ir proxies where detectable.
SEM-BSE/EDS of candidate inclusions and metal-glass boundaries.
LA-ICP-MS or micro-PIXE/appropriate trace-element method for Au, Ag, Cu, Ni, Co, Pt, Ir, Ga and Ge.
Analyze unshocked local sandstone/colluvium controls from the same stratigraphic units.
Blind-classify inclusions as TARGET-LIKE, PROJECTILE-LIKE, MIXED or ANTHROPOGENIC-CANDIDATE before applying Osiris/pyramid semantics.

reverse_pass.BACK: Assume the gold predates the impact; ask what material signature must survive after melting.
reverse_pass.FORWARD: Target-derived Au should appear in target-dominated white glass or unshocked target without requiring Ni-rich projectile contamination.
reverse_pass.LEFT: Natural terrestrial gold and anthropogenic worked gold are separate hypotheses and must not be merged.
reverse_pass.RIGHT: Meteorite Au at 1.57 ppm is retained as the compulsory background control, not as the preferred interpretation.
reverse_pass.FORWARD_AGAIN: Use elemental covariance and metallurgical morphology to assign source before interpreting meaning.
reverse_pass.BACK_AGAIN: A gold inclusion becomes archaeologically interesting only if its source is inconsistent with the projectile and ordinary target background.
